plants.opening_line: MaiCo's equipment page says it has more than 40 Lincoln DC600 MIG welding machines, and a KansasWorks welder posting dated July 29, 2026 was still live on November 12, 2026; could automated welding on its multi-sided poles take some of that load?

Nello's site says it launched a campus expansion in 2025 that brings its facilities to over 320,000 square feet, its careers page lists Welder and Sub-arc seam welder openings, and its manufacturing page says AWS D1.1 qualified teams work alongside automated robotic cells; which welds are still done by hand?

PennFab's equipment page lists a Panasonic robot welding system, its blog says it uses flux core, sub-arc and gas metal arc welding, and its careers page has an opening for a welder with MIG experience; how is welding split today between the robot and your manual welders?

A 2018 SteelOrbis report on Valmont's acquisition of Walpar said the Birmingham, Alabama facility had served the transportation market since 1974 and employed about 70 people, and described Walpar as an industry leader in manufacturing overhead sign structures.

A Valmont Fitter posting for Claremore, Oklahoma, shown as posted about two years before November 2026, said the job builds and welds poles with GMAW to AWS D1.1 on products up to 120 inches in diameter and 80,000 lb; are parts still that large?
A Valmont Welder 4 posting listed for McCook, Nebraska asks for six months to one year of hands-on MIG welding experience in a production environment.

Valmont Brenham pole-line postings, all removed by January 2026, described fitters tack-welding small components to pole shafts with GMAW or FCAW from drawings, with SAW for structural welds; could an autonomous cell take on that fit-and-weld step?

A Valmont Newmark Columbus, Nebraska welder posting, now marked inactive, asked for at least five years of MIG welding experience for steel electrical poles and substation structures; an autonomous cell could cut how much of that experience each shift needs.
Sabre announced in 2017 that its Bossier City plant would add a production line for large steel transmission poles and 50 new jobs.

Arcosa Traffic Structures' website says it is an AISC/AWS Certified Fabricator that manufactures tolling gantries, overhead sign structures, and mast arm and steel strain poles, and an expired, undated Entry Fitter/Welder posting for Sumterville, Florida asked for MIG welding experience with flux core preferred.

A Meyer Utility Structures posting for a Plant Welding Engineer at its Lancaster, SC operation (now expired, undated) asked for advanced knowledge of FCAW, SAW and GMAW and listed duties to revamp the in-plant welding schools and maintain welder defect-rate metrics.

A 2011 Area Development item said Ameron was building a 75,000-square-foot facility in Tulsa, Oklahoma, to produce steel poles, and the nov.com pole products page says Ameron Pole Products LLC is a subsidiary of Arcosa, Inc.; confirm which Tulsa site makes poles today.
MICA Steelworks' careers page advertises a signing bonus for welders and fitters, and a Haltom City welder posting (date not shown) lists proficiency with flux core and metal core wire.

Di Highway's capabilities page says its welders use the flux core welding process to AWS D1.5, and its overhead sign structures page says they are designed to span up to 240 feet; how are you handling the variety of designs across those jobs?
